title: Machine learning & AI
blurb: Learning systems built and measured end to end — from NumPy-only models to an offline speech pipeline.

projects.title: Machine learning from first principles
projects.role: Four learners written in NumPy only, each tuned and reported against a hidden test set
points: ECG rhythm classifier — softmax logistic regression over hand-designed features from raw single-lead ECG (PhysioNet/CinC 2017 task: normal, AF, other), comparing four gradient-descent variants and class-weighting against focal loss for the imbalance.

Neural networks for Indic language identification — fully connected networks trained from scratch on audio features for Hindi-vs-Bengali and a 10-language task, with a study of activation, loss (cross-entropy vs MSE), learning-rate schedule and optimiser (SGD, RMSprop, Adam).

Prompt-safety text classifier — Bernoulli and multinomial Naive Bayes over 927,760 prompts, with stopword-threshold and n-gram-selection sweeps that lifted validation accuracy past the required margin.
Maximum-margin sparse networks — neural network with an SVM output layer, then sparsified (in progress).

projects.title: Offline Hindi–Gujarati speech translation
points: Fully offline speech-to-speech pipeline: Vosk for ASR, AI4Bharat for translation and Meta MMS-TTS for synthesis, stitched together multi-threaded.
End-to-end latency around 800 ms on CPU and 450 ms on GPU for medium-length sentences.
About 97% accuracy on the tested sentence set.

projects.title: Search and adversarial planning
projects.role: Two AI course projects — game playing and constrained scheduling
points: Stones & Rivers game agent — minimax search over a two-player strategy game, with board evaluation heuristics capturing positional and tactical features and learned weights guiding the tree search.

Flood relief supply planner — relief delivery modelled as constrained optimisation, scheduling multi-trip helicopter routes to maximise supply delivered to remote villages within time and weight bounds.

title: Systems & performance
blurb: Code close to the machine, each with a measured baseline: a query engine, a language runtime, SIMD, CUDA and MPI.

projects.title: Memory-bounded TPC-H query engine
points: Query execution engine running multi-gigabyte TPC-H workloads under a strict 64 MB memory budget.
Volcano-model iterator pipeline with external merge sort and an LRU buffer pool.
Cost-based join selection, with a memory-aware fallback to disk-based joins.

projects.title: Custom language runtime
projects.role: Shell, compiler, virtual machine, debugger and garbage collector
points: Mini-shell with command pipelines, background processes and job control.
ptrace-based debugger with software breakpoints and register inspection.
Flex/Bison compiler targeting a stack-based virtual machine, with its own assembler and a garbage collector.
All five components integrated behind one shell — compile, run and debug in a single session.

projects.title: GEMM and Smith–Waterman acceleration
points: Dense matrix multiplication tuned with AVX-512 vectorisation, cache blocking, loop unrolling and memory alignment — 44.31 GFLOP/s and a 2.18× speedup over the NumPy baseline, from 1K×1K to 12K×12K.
Smith–Waterman alignment parallelised by anti-diagonal wavefront with AVX-512 and OpenMP — 23× over the C baseline.
Both measured on a 4-core CPU against single-threaded references.

projects.title: GPU local histogram equalisation
points: CUDA kernels for local histogram equalisation, with KNN and K-Means neighbourhood search traded off for speed against accuracy.
On NVIDIA Kepler (sm_35) against a sequential baseline: 16.87× with K-Means, 11.44× with KNN.

projects.title: Distributed budgeted maximum-weight clique
points: Branch-and-bound solver distributed across MPI ranks, with non-blocking bound sharing to prune redundant branches as they appear.
Graph colouring for upper-bound pruning and fractional knapsack for budget feasibility.
6.87× speedup at 12 processes.

title: Security & applications
blurb: A cipher benchmarked on a microcontroller, and a small web service built on third-party APIs.

projects.title: DNA-based lightweight cipher for IoT
points: Implemented and benchmarked a DNA-based lightweight block cipher against established lightweight designs.
Extended it with a 4-round structure, additive modular substitution and a row-diffusion cascade — avalanche effect from 1.56% to 35.0%, key sensitivity from 8.33% to 49.66%.
43.3 KB/s encryption throughput on an Arduino Uno, ahead of PRESENT and LEA.

projects.title: Minutes Away
projects.role: Nearby places ranked by real travel time, not map distance
points: Flask service that calls Google Places (New) for candidates, then Routes v2 concurrently for each candidate, and ranks by minutes rather than metres.
Keys stay server-side; a distance-only fallback keeps the page usable when routing fails. Nine place categories and four travel modes.
